events.content:
Done — the title is now part of the prefetched shell, while the project details are excluded from prefetching and stream in only when you actually navigate. I verified this against a production build by inspecting the prefetch and navigation payloads.

**What I changed**

1. **`app/projects/[slug]/page.tsx`** — split the single Suspense boundary into two. Before, the title and details were awaited together with `Promise.all`, so the prefetchable shell was just the "Loading project..." fallback and the title couldn't appear until the 800ms details fetch finished. Now `<ProjectTitle>` and `<ProjectDetails>` sit in separate boundaries, so the title can resolve independently.

2. **`lib/data.ts`** — added `cacheLife({ stale: 0 })` inside `getProjectDetails`. With Cache Components, `<Link>` prefetching includes every `'use cache'` result in the prefetched payload by default — so despite the Suspense split, the details would still have been prefetched. A cached entry is only included in prefetches when its `stale` time is at least 30 seconds (`MIN_PREFETCHABLE_STALE` in the Next.js source); below that, it's omitted and becomes a dynamic hole filled at navigation. `getProjectTitle` keeps the default profile, so it stays prefetchable. The details remain server-side cached (default 15-minute revalidate), so navigations after the first are still fast — the data just isn't shipped ahead of time.

**Verification** (production build, `next start`):
- Runtime prefetch request (`Next-Router-Prefetch: 2`) for `/projects/orbit` returned the payload with **"Orbit Analytics" and the "Loading details" fallback, but no details content**.
- A real navigation request returned both title and details.
- Build succeeds with the route reported as Partial Prerender, and `tsc --noEmit` is clean.

So on navigation the title renders instantly from the prefetched data, the details fallback shows briefly, and the activity list streams in.
